findings.title: Settled-provider cleanup and final tuple checks do not cover every continuation
findings.rationale: Static residual of the approved per-binding holder/current-tuple contract, SCOPE-04/DOD-03/VAL-03 and CP2-UNCERTAINTY/CANCEL/RECEIPT; not evidence of duplicate POST or lost accepted receipt. The original first-POST history race, competing promotion CAS and binding-wide lease/cooldown are materially repaired. providerCall571-623 now releases its exact token after a settled provider exception or its own rejected success revalidation; run12 supports the repaired receipt/cancel error and both successor-holder success/error cases. However, after providerCall returns normally, subscribeAfterMapping552 awaits another requireSubscriptionOrReceipt and553-565 runs another finalization transaction; either can reject or roll back before releaseBindingOperation566, with no finally covering them. The observation-null transaction523-540 likewise can throw before release541. Thus a successfully settled HTTP request followed by a final DB/actor/expiry failure retains its original binding holder until lease expiry. The existing recovery trigger targets later confirmation_state=COMPLETED, after566, so it does not exercise this path. Additionally, the observation-null transaction locks resources but527-531 updates only the attempt/session/attempt-lease tuple; it does not revalidate current binding token, generation or credential version after the preceding providerCall check. A takeover between that check and this transaction can therefore still mutate the old attempt. The current takeover tests cover a POST returning true or throwing inside providerCall, not this successful GET/null continuation.

Never release while HTTP is still pending. Revalidate the exact current binding/channel/generation/credential tuple in the observation finalization transaction before its attempt mutation. Add a real PostgreSQL fault on the post-POST subscription-finalization write, disable it before recovery, and prove original-holder cleanup with unchanged known facts/at-most-onePOST.
